title: The Practical and Contemplative Life in Psalm 118
english: The legal and prophetic writers and even the words of God's new covenant are given naked of types. For, exercising themselves through them and being led according to their spiritual will, we reach the point of meeting face to face with the truth. If the beginning of those bearing them is the truth itself and they become so because of it, and if God's words also bear toward the truth (for they are spoken because of it), it is rightly said that their beginning is the truth. Since also that which exists in some is called a beginning by another meaning, and truth exists in God's words, they are themselves true by that, and because of this they are called their beginning. Similarly, the true state is held to be upon the true words, by which the divinely-breathed scriptures—which are the words of God—are said to be from self-truth. And because of this, it is right to say that the truth is the beginning of God's words.

And what is it? Since the Lord says, 'I am the truth,' the word of God is also that itself; he says to the Father, 'Your word is truth,' who becomes with each prophet. And likewise: those established according to the truth, being truth-receivers, become the beginning of God's words. Just as the truth was the beginning of your words, so all your judgments of justice are found indestructible and shown forever (Ps 118:161c).

Cowardice is twofold: one part is the irrational regarding the emotional part of the soul, the other is the logical established regarding the heart and the intellect, not of reason, and perhaps it can pertain to the same divine fear. Throughout his life, the righteous man, being enlightened, will be in a perfect day not intercepted by night and will praise God sevenfold (Ps 118:164), having become transcendent to be separated from the world that has become in days of exile, even having been in God's paradise, having contemplated the word of God's creation and providence, will confess the judgments of the justice of God, according to the judgments of each varied creation and providence. If he also awaits the Savior, as it is said, 'All flesh shall see the salvation of God' (Ps 118:166), following this he loves the commandments of God.
And he has expected salvation, so that both his practice is pure and his expectation is contemplative, always expecting and contemplating that God has come to seek and to save the lost.

He prays for such a worthy condition to be tested, certain and unshakeable, as if to enter before the Lord. 'And I will know if my worthiness enters before you, if I am rescued by you according to your word and your wisdom' (Ps 118:170). For He, being above all passions, irrational and the evils working from irrationality, having departed from them, is rescued by God according to His word.

'Oh that you would teach me, so that I might act from it and know them clearly; I would bring to you a thankful hymn from my lips, O Lord, of your man' (Ps 118:171). If the impulse of hymnody to God is clearly the beginning of its nourishment, it constitutes full theology.

'Your various commandments are instructions; they all possess the virtues of those who are wise, the general virtue being to follow the particular virtues, as one possessing the one perfectly possesses all' (Ps 118:172). 'I utter your word with my lips toward your man' (Ps 118:173a). But the word concerning righteousness is uttered principally not by voice alone, not by merely bringing it forth, but also by works and by practical intention, being corrected according to the right word.

'Let your hand be done to save me' (Ps 118:174a) does not signify here the generation of it according to essence, but the relation toward the ones being saved. The same thought is carried in 'Become for me a protector toward God'. The path of the one longing for the salvation of God is the one who has the study of the law as his desire, pre-sounding his arrival here. By 'law' he calls here the ancient and divine Scripture.

'Since remembering your judgments and being set apart, I turn away from the death that follows sin' (Ps 118:175). Not merely sinning, but performing those things, which follow the living of the soul and the praising of you thankfully, through which you provide it with immortal life. Since remembering your judgments, I turn away from the death following sin by not sinning; my soul shall live, having worked out those of life and praising the thankful ones, through which you provide it with immortal life.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Ascent to the Temple and the Kingdom
english: Having lost a sheep from the hundred, the Savior comes seeking it, having left the ninety-nine in the wilderness; the human race has gone astray through Adam's transgression. The human race is the lost sheep from the hundred, while the rational things that do not stumble remain part of creation in the desert, staying high in virtue and truth, except for man who has gone into error.

Therefore, like the sheep, but rather a part of it, [the Psalmist says]: 'I have gone astray; seek me, your servant; for you came to seek and save the lost; seek me so that you may find me ready for this; for I have longed for your commandments' (Ps 119). It is to be understood that he in the Jerusalem temple has fifteen steps, and standing on each of them, those appointed to sing hymns were saying an ode. Therefore, the number of odes coincided with the steps. The arrangement concerning the odes and those singing them on each step of the temple lies in the Chronicles.

You shall understand the temple of God to be a holy, intelligible, and spiritual thing—the theology—and the steps to be the stages of progress. He who has ascended to the second step of the temple begins to be transformed into perfection, no longer thinking of something lowly. Therefore, he says he has lifted the eyes of the intellect toward the height. Thus, the ode of the second step has attained a familiar number. For the one hundred and twentieth limits the perfection of human life.

Indeed, it has been said concerning men after the flood: 'Their days shall be [one hundred and twenty]' (Gen 6:3). Thus also Moses, the great hierophant and servant of God, having perfected human life into one hundred and twenty years, describes his own life, setting forth his own life as a pattern for those under him who receive the laws. It can also be strongly understood regarding the exodus: the exodus of God guarding from evil for one turning away from evil, and likewise the exodus of one guarding the doing of the good, an exodus from the sensible toward the intelligible and spiritual. He who...

He who stretches himself forward toward those before him does not forget them, nor does he run back again. For he who hastens toward the prize of the higher calling goes toward the higher things. Therefore, having begun the ascent toward the temple, he does not return after having traveled; having ascended to the third degree, he does not even depart from the flight of the soul, but, having received a vision, he hastens toward that which he is being urged to lead the entrance of, being in good spirit.

Those having firmly established the feet of their own souls previously in the courts of Jerusalem (Ps 121:2–4), have a desire also to ascend to the temple. And the most sharp-witted theology is the temple, while the partial contemplations are the courts of the vision of peace, the specific virtues that occur. The vision of the aforementioned peace, having begun to be transformed, becomes as a city built by the Lord, and its participation consists of the same aforementioned courts, in which the feet of the firm ones are standing. And it is not a low-lying thing, but exists in some height, so that the citizen who wishes to become of it does not descend, but ascends toward it.

And indeed, the various ranks of the saved, having the choice of confession, ascend there as watches of the Lord, having been well testified by the Lord to ascend and having confessed, and they increase in zeal and progress, doing these things, Israel. David the savior has said many things (Ps 121:5); therefore, because it is from the seed of David, it is according to the flesh, and because it is sufficiently by hand, it is so; for David is interpreted as being 'capable by hand.' For how is he not capable by hand, he who performs wondrous powers? This is the church of David, in which thrones are seen for judgment, upon which the apostles sit judging the twelve tribes of Israel. For the faith and the citizenship of each apostle is a throne of his kingdom, judging and condemning those who have not conformed to what is prophesied in the divine scriptures, nor believed in those whom he made and taught with words.

title: Stability of Faith and the Heavenly Zion
english: Jerusalem, because she reigns with power, has become peaceful, having previously been at war with enemies whom she overcomes by her might, finding tranquility in her high towers. For the great towers in the walls are being constructed for the purpose of watching for the coming enemies. For among the Syrians, large houses are called heavy dwellings, and some, having taken height upon the walled cities, having their position, are called high towers. Therefore, Jerusalem, having used her own power which is from God, has subjected those who oppose her; she will make peace, and tranquility will follow in her high towers.

If, however, in allegory, the high towers are those who, through the height of the commonwealth and the vision of the truth, not only watch for the enemies coming for war but also cast them down from on high in reproofs. According to the vision, he who is born from God, doing righteousness and believing that Jesus is the Christ, has brothers who perform the same things and believe, and neighbors who approach through the doing of righteousness and the faith of Jesus Christ.

But since of both these ranks, of his brothers and of his neighbors, I say that Jerusalem, who is to be given, says she speaks peace and is peaceful (Ps 122:8,9), I wish for them, both the brothers and the neighbors of the fatherland, but since they seek the goods of the Lord their God, seeking the truly good things for Jerusalem. For he says concerning the one who began to ascend (Ps 122:2), since seeking the good things for Jerusalem, the keeping of the divine commandments and the right understanding of the true faith.

It is possible for slaves having eyes to take into the hands of masters the nations which are being managed under the angels, according to how the nations stood according to the number of the angels of God; but the circumcision assembly having eyes, a little girl into the hands of the mistress, a little girl because she is called a spirit of slavery; but her mistress, calling the unblemished and spotless church of God, no one stumbles. But we do not have [our eyes] in the hands of those masters, but we approach to the Lord our God for mercy.

And [it] shows mercy to us (Ps 123:4a). The Ara does not speak in a way that is merely formal, but in a way that is collective. An unsubstantial gift is one that is possible to receive without Christ sustaining it. If someone signifies evil as an unsubstantial gift, it must be said that evil is called unsubstantial because it lacks essence and its own subsistence; for it does not exist as a substance in those who are acting, not having its own nature.

Just as the mountain of Zion is unshakable and immovable (for the Word of God is [it]), so also those trusting in God have an immovable standing, imitating Him as they hasten to be. For the upcoming text is not said regarding the sensible mountain, similarly to all those mountains that are steadfast, but regarding that [mountain] about which the Spirit commands the prophet, saying, 'Ascend upon a high mountain, O you who preach Zion.' For Zion, being interpreted as the watchtower of the holy Church's contemplation of good things, is the high mountain; and regarding the mountain of the heavenly Zion, it is said, 'But you have come to the mountain of Zion and to the city of the living God, Jerusalem the heavenly' (Ps 125:2). Let us therefore establish the trust toward God, so as to chance upon both blessedness and the other promises, as the prophecy exhorts us: 'And having trusted in the Lord, He will lift you up upon the good things of the earth' (Ps 124:1). For the beginning of being lifted up upon the good things of the earth of the living and gentle ones is to have trusted in Him.

As for the Church, it is seen being enriched in the 'Shine, shine, Jerusalem, Jerusalem built as a city.' Therefore, he who thinks perfectly and genuinely that the things of the Church will dwell in it forever will not be shaken, nor will he be removed from this habitation, having received the things to be practiced and thought about with certainty and immovability. And it will be said specifically that he dwells in it forever, the living one and the believing one in the Lord, who shall not die forever, having here received the pledge of eternal life. But if he should ever become negligent, as if it were possible through attention and desire for the good, the habitation will be moved; for this reason it says in Proverbs, 'A righteous man will not be moved forever' (Prov 10:25).
